nodes.summary: Let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable, mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, each with the same distribution as $X_0$, where $X_0$ has a finite third moment, mean $\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$ and variance $\sigma^2 = \operatorname{Var}(X_0) > 0$ with $\sigma > 0$. Write $\rho = \mathbb{E}|X_0|^3$, $S_n = X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1}$, and $\Phi$ for the distribution function of the standard normal…
nodes.title: Berry–Esseen theorem with constant 42

nodes.summary: Let $(\xi_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ be measurable, mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, and let $s$ be a finite set of indices such that for each $j \in s$ the variable $\xi_j$ has a finite third moment and mean $\mathbb{E}[\xi_j] = 0$, and such that $\sum_{j \in s} \mathbb{E}[\xi_j^2] = 1$. Write $\Phi$ for the distribution function of the standard normal distribution. If $\gamma \ge 0$…
nodes.title: Berry–Esseen bound for finite sums

nodes.summary: There is a constant $C > 0$ with the following property. Let $X_0, X_1, X_2, \dots$ be measurable, mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, each with the same distribution as $X_0$, where $X_0$ is integrable and has a finite third moment, mean $\mathbb{E}[X_0] = 0$ and variance $\sigma^2 = \operatorname{Var}(X_0) > 0$ with $\sigma > 0$. Write $\rho = \mathbb{E}|X_0|^3$,…
nodes.title: Berry–Esseen theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $n$ be a positive integer, let $F$ be the cumulative distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$, and let $\Phi$ be the standard normal cumulative distribution function. Then for every real $a$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$ is at most $a$ if and only if $|F(x) - \Phi(x)| \le a$ for every real $x$.
nodes.title: Kolmogorov error bounds are uniform CDF bounds

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, let $n$ be a positive integer, let $F$ be the cumulative distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$, and let $\Phi$ be the standard normal cumulative distribution function. Then the set $\{|F(x) - \Phi(x)| : x \in \mathbb{R}\}$ is bounded above.
nodes.title: The CDF errors are bounded above

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$ and let $i$ be a natural number. The coordinate map $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ under the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ and the identity map of $\mathbb{R}$ under $\mu$ are identically distributed.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the i.i.d. product are distributed like the original law

nodes.summary: If $\mu$ is a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$, then the coordinate maps $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$, for $i \in \mathbb{N}$, are mutually independent under the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the i.i.d. product are independent

nodes.summary: If $\mu$ is a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$ and $i$ is a natural number, then the pushforward of the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ under the coordinate map $\omega \mapsto \omega_i$ from $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ to $\mathbb{R}$ is $\mu$.
nodes.title: Coordinate laws of the i.i.d. product

nodes.summary: If $\mu$ is a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$, then the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ is a probability measure.
nodes.title: The i.i.d. product of a standardized law is a probability measure

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the i.i.d. product law of $\mu$ is the measure on the sequence space $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ that is the infinite product $\mu^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ of countably many copies of $\mu$ when $\mu$ is a probability measure, and the zero measure otherwise.
nodes.title: I.i.d. product law

nodes.summary: Let $\Omega$ be a measurable space with a measure $P$, and let $(X_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be real-valued functions on $\Omega$. They form a standardized i.i.d. model when $P$ is a probability measure, every $X_i$ is measurable, the $X_i$ are mutually independent under $P$, every $X_i$ has the same law under $P$ as $X_0$, and $X_0$ has mean $\int_\Omega X_0 \, dP = 0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment…
nodes.title: Standardized i.i.d. models

nodes.summary: A measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is a standardized law when it is a probability measure with mean $\int x \, d\mu(x) = 0$ and variance $1$, and has finite third absolute moment $\int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x) < \infty$.
nodes.title: Standardized laws with finite third moment

nodes.summary: If $(X_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a standardized i.i.d. model on a measurable space $\Omega$ with measure $P$, then the law under $P$ of the sequence map $\omega \mapsto (X_i(\omega))_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ equals the i.i.d. product law of the law of $X_0$ under $P$.
nodes.title: The joint law of a standardized i.i.d. model

nodes.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every positive integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$, that is $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)|$ where $F_{\mu,n}$ is Mathlib's cumulative distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ and $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function, is at most $1$.
nodes.title: The Kolmogorov error is at most one

nodes.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and every positive integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$, that is $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)|$ where $F_{\mu,n}$ is Mathlib's cumulative distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ and $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function, is nonnegative.
nodes.title: The Kolmogorov error is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a positive integer $n$, the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$ is the real supremum $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)|$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and $F_{\mu,n}$ is Mathlib's cumulative distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$. When $\mu$ is a probability measure, $F_{\mu,n}(x)$ is the mass the…
nodes.title: Kolmogorov error

nodes.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the identity function $x \mapsto x$ belongs to $L^3(\mu)$ if and only if the function $x \mapsto |x|^3$ is $\mu$-integrable.
nodes.title: Finite third absolute moment as an $L^3$ condition

nodes.summary: For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $\Phi(x)$ is the value at $x$ of the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, that is, the probability that a standard normal random variable is at most $x$.
nodes.title: Standard normal CDF

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$ (a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment), let $n$ be a positive integer and let $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the cumulative distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$, evaluated at $x$, equals the probability under the i.i.d. law $\mu^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of the event…
nodes.title: CDF of the normalized sum

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a probability measure on a measurable space $\Omega$ and let $X_0, X_1, \dots$ be real random variables on $\Omega$ that are measurable, independent and identically distributed under $P$, with $X_0$ of mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then for every positive integer $n$, the law under $P$ of $(X_0 + \dots + X_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$ equals the normalized law at $n$ of the law of $X_0$.
nodes.title: Normalized sums of an i.i.d. model have the canonical law

nodes.summary: For every standardized law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ (a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment), the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n = 1$ is $\mu$ itself.
nodes.title: The normalized law with one summand

nodes.summary: For every standardized law $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ (a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment) and every positive integer $n$, the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ is a probability measure.
nodes.title: The normalized law is a probability measure

nodes.summary: For a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and a positive integer $n$, the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ is the pushforward of the i.i.d. law of $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ (the product measure $\mu^{\otimes \mathbb{N}}$ when $\mu$ is a probability measure, and the zero measure otherwise) under the normalized sum $\omega \mapsto (\omega_0 + \dots + \omega_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$.
nodes.title: Law of the normalized sum

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $n$, the map sending a real sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$ to $(\omega_0 + \dots + \omega_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$ is measurable with respect to the product $\sigma$-algebra on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$.
nodes.title: Measurability of the normalized sum

nodes.summary: For a positive integer $n$ and a real sequence $\omega = (\omega_0, \omega_1, \dots)$, the normalized sum $S_n(\omega)$ is the sum of the first $n$ coordinates divided by $\sqrt{n}$: $S_n(\omega) = (\omega_0 + \dots + \omega_{n-1})/\sqrt{n}$.
nodes.title: Normalized sum

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, $n$ a positive integer and $x$ a real number. Let $F_{\mu,n}$ be the distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ and $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function. Then $|F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)| \le 1$.
nodes.title: The CDF error is at most one

nodes.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$, $n$ a positive integer, $F_{\mu,n}$ the distribution function of the normalized law of $\mu$ at $n$ and $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function. Then for every real $x$, $|F_{\mu,n}(x) - \Phi(x)| \le \sup_{y \in \mathbb{R}} |F_{\mu,n}(y) - \Phi(y)|$, the right side being the Kolmogorov error of $\mu$ at $n$.
nodes.title: Each CDF error is at most the Kolmogorov error

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be the distribution function of the normalized law of the standard normal law $N(0,1)$ at $n = 1$, and $\Phi$ the standard normal distribution function. Then the Kolmogorov error of $N(0,1)$ at $n = 1$, $\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} |F(x) - \Phi(x)|$, equals $0$.
nodes.title: The Kolmogorov error vanishes for one standard Gaussian summand

nodes.summary: The standard normal law $N(0,1)$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is a standardized law: it is a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment.
nodes.title: The standard Gaussian is a standardized law

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$ and $X_0, X_1, \dots$ real-valued functions on $\Omega$ forming an i.i.d. model: $P$ is a probability measure, the $X_i$ are measurable, independent and identically distributed, and $X_0$ has mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then the law of $X_0$, the pushforward of $P$ under $X_0$, is a standardized law.
nodes.title: The common law of an i.i.d. model is standardized

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a measure on a measurable space $\Omega$ and $X_0, X_1, \dots$ real-valued functions on $\Omega$ forming an i.i.d. model: $P$ is a probability measure, the $X_i$ are measurable, independent and identically distributed, and $X_0$ has mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment. Then the third absolute moment of the law of $X_0$ equals $\int_\Omega |X_0(\omega)|^3 \, dP(\omega)$.
nodes.title: Third absolute moment of the common law

nodes.summary: If $\mu$ is a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$, then the function $x \mapsto |x|^3$ is integrable with respect to $\mu$.
nodes.title: Standardized laws have an integrable third absolute moment

nodes.summary: For every measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, the third absolute moment $\int_{\mathbb{R}} |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$ is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the third absolute moment

nodes.summary: If $\mu$ is a standardized law on $\mathbb{R}$, that is, a probability measure with mean $0$, variance $1$ and finite third absolute moment, then its third absolute moment $\int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$ is strictly positive.
nodes.title: The third absolute moment of a standardized law is positive

nodes.summary: The third absolute moment of a measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is the real number $\int |x|^3 \, d\mu(x)$, taken to be $0$ when $x \mapsto |x|^3$ is not integrable with respect to $\mu$.
nodes.title: Third absolute moment

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
